findings.issue_text: Embeddable host CRUD adapter pathFor() unconditionally returns '/admin/customize/embedding', so create/update/destroy requests hit the wrong URL and 404; should only override pathFor for the 'embedding' type

Migration string-interpolates host values directly into INSERT SQL, so values containing quotes break the SQL; values should be quoted/parameterized
Admin embeddable_hosts controller update/destroy raises NoMethodError (500) when record is missing instead of returning 404, reachable via stale admin tabs
Embedding controller update ignores params and persists nothing while returning success, so the 'Save changes' button is a silent no-op masking lost input
record_for_host returns false as a 'not found' sentinel instead of nil, conflating malformed URI with not-found and creating sentinel-value hazard for callers
Embeddable-host component sets host.category from stale empty categoryId after save, so UI shows no category until reload when backend defaults category_id
host_allowed? runs an uncacheable lower(host) = ? SQL lookup per embed request, replacing the memoized site setting check and adding per-view DB cost on a hot path

Host is never lowercased before save, so lower() does real work; a functional index on lower(host) or normalized lowercase storage with a plain unique index would fix this
record_for_host called per TopicEmbed.import lookup (app/models/topic_embed.rb:36), running a fresh host lookup query before PostCreator, inheriting the missing-index problem

Migration crashes on sites without an `embed_category` setting: `execute(...)[0]['id']` in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11` is called before any nil guard, raising NoMethodError when the site_settings row is absent and aborting the migration

RestAdapter's `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore, so multi-word admin models (e.g. site_customization) silently fall out of ADMIN_MODELS and hit the non-admin base path — fragile change to the shared RestAdapter.basePath contract
`PUT /admin/customize/embedding` update action fetches and re-renders but never persists anything, making it a silent no-op that returns 200 OK while discarding request bodies

`_hydrateEmbedded` in `store.js.es6` now matches any `*_ids` key on every model, deleting raw ids and replacing them with a junk array (e.g. [undefined]) when the subtype isn't registered — shape drift for existing consumers; delete should be conditional on successful hydration
`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` yields nil for unknown ids and then calls `host.host = ...` / `host.destroy` on nil, producing NoMethodError 500s instead of 404s

Migration inserts unescaped host strings via raw SQL interpolation in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25-27`; a host value containing a single quote breaks or corrupts the migration

Serializer exposes only `category_id` while the client reconstructs `host.category` ad-hoc via `Discourse.Category.findById`, leaving an implicit contract for external consumers of `/admin/embeddable_hosts`

Migration crashes with NoMethodError on sites without an 'embed_category' site setting, as execute(...)[0]['id'] indexes nil when the result set is empty (same pattern for uncategorized_category_id and embeddable_hosts[0]['value'] lookups); guard each execute result for zero rows before indexing

SQL injection / corrupt data in migration: INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts interpolates the raw site-setting host value into SQL; a host containing a single quote breaks or corrupts the migration; use quote or parameterized inserts

Migration inserts host values verbatim without normalization (e.g. 'http://eviltrout.com'), but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) against the URI host and before_validation never runs for migration-inserted rows, so embedding silently breaks for sites with protocol/path in configured hosts; migration must strip protocol/path the same way the model does

Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embeddable host CRUD adapter pathFor() unconditionally returns '/admin/customize/embedding', so create/update/destroy requests hit the wrong URL and 404; should only override pathFor for the 'embedding' type

adjudication.rationale: The only adapter added is `app/assets/javascripts/admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6`, which overrides `pathFor()` for the **embedding** model to `/admin/customize/embedding`. There is no `embeddable-host` adapter overriding `pathFor()`. CRUD for `embeddable-host` will use the standard REST paths under `/admin/` (supported by the change to `ADMIN_MODELS` including `'embeddable-host'` and the new Rails `resources :embeddable_hosts` route), not `/admin/customize/embedding`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on fresh installs with NoMethodError because execute("...WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'] dereferences nil when no embed_category row exists, blocking all deploys
Migration string-interpolates host values directly into INSERT SQL, so values containing quotes break the SQL; values should be quoted/parameterized

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds raw SQL with direct string interpolation of each host value: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If `h` contains a single quote (or other special characters), this will break the SQL and could potentially allow SQL injection. The values should be properly quoted/escaped or inserted via parameterization/ActiveRecord APIs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embeddable_hosts controller update/destroy raises NoMethodError (500) when record is missing instead of returning 404, reachable via stale admin tabs
Embedding controller update ignores params and persists nothing while returning success, so the 'Save changes' button is a silent no-op masking lost input

adjudication.rationale: The new PUT endpoint `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` is wired up, but `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` ignores request params and performs no persistence (it just re-renders the `@embedding` OpenStruct). On the client, `admin-embedding` controller’s `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which will hit this no-op update route and appear to succeed while changing nothing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host returns false as a 'not found' sentinel instead of nil, conflating malformed URI with not-found and creating sentinel-value hazard for callers

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, `record_for_host` returns `false` when the URI is malformed or has no host (`return false unless uri.present?` / `return false unless host.present?`), but returns `nil` when the lookup misses (`where(...).first`). This inconsistent sentinel (`false` vs `nil`) can be a caller hazard and blurs “invalid input” vs “not found”, even though current callers mostly use `.present?`/`.try` and won’t break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embeddable-host component sets host.category from stale empty categoryId after save, so UI shows no category until reload when backend defaults category_id

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` the `save()` action sets `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')`. If the user leaves the chooser blank, `categoryId` stays `null`. The backend (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) explicitly defaults blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, so the saved record will have a real category. However, after the save resolves, the component unconditionally does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));` which with `null` will set `host.category` to `undefined`/empty, causing the UI (`{{category-badge host.category}}`) to show no category until a reload/refetch hydrates it from `category_id`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: host_allowed? runs an uncacheable lower(host) = ? SQL lookup per embed request, replacing the memoized site setting check and adding per-view DB cost on a hot path

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the previous SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? check with EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? in hot paths (e.g., EmbedController#ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever#invalid_host?). host_allowed? calls record_for_host, which performs a DB query `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` each time. The new migration creates `embeddable_hosts` without adding an index on `host`, and using `lower(host)` can also prevent use of a normal index even if one existed. This is a concrete performance/architecture regression (extra per-request DB work), not a functional correctness bug shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator files are swapped: category_fabricator.rb defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) and vice versa, fragile against load-order assumptions

New DB query on hot embed path (EmbeddableHost lookup in ensure_embeddable) per request with no index on host and lower(host) = ? query causes a full table scan per request on a high-traffic public endpoint, regressing from cached SiteSetting behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` to call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), which performs a DB lookup via `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). The migration creating `embeddable_hosts` does not add an index on `host` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb), and the query uses `lower(host)` so even a plain index wouldn’t be used without a functional index. This introduces a per-request DB query on a public embed endpoint, representing a concrete performance/scalability concern compared to the previous in-memory `SiteSetting` check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host is never lowercased before save, so lower() does real work; a functional index on lower(host) or normalized lowercase storage with a plain unique index would fix this

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost` the `before_validation` callback strips scheme/path but does not normalize case (`app/models/embeddable_host.rb`), while lookups use `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` (`record_for_host`). That means every lookup applies `lower()` on the column and there is no supporting index shown in the migration (`create_embeddable_hosts` creates no index/unique constraint). This is a performance/data-normalization concern (and could enable case-variant duplicates), but it’s not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff because the lookup still works correctly via `lower(host)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host called per TopicEmbed.import lookup (app/models/topic_embed.rb:36), running a fresh host lookup query before PostCreator, inheriting the missing-index problem

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) and `record_for_host` queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). The new migration creating `embeddable_hosts` does not add an index on `host` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb), so this introduces a likely performance concern (table scans on embed operations), but not a direct correctness/security defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on sites without an `embed_category` setting: `execute(...)[0]['id']` in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11` is called before any nil guard, raising NoMethodError when the site_settings row is absent and aborting the migration

RestAdapter's `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore, so multi-word admin models (e.g. site_customization) silently fall out of ADMIN_MODELS and hit the non-admin base path — fragile change to the shared RestAdapter.basePath contract

adjudication.rationale: In `RestAdapter.basePath`, the new check is `type.replace('_', '-')`, which indeed only replaces the first underscore. However, the finding’s concrete example (`site_customization`) does not demonstrate the problem: it has only one underscore, so it *will* correctly become `site-customization`, matching `ADMIN_MODELS` as changed in the diff. The claim that this makes existing multi-word admin models “silently fall out” is not verifiable from the diff (no admin model shown with multiple underscores), so the reported broken behavior is speculative/misread.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` update action fetches and re-renders but never persists anything, making it a silent no-op that returns 200 OK while discarding request bodies

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`, the action simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` after `fetch_embedding` builds an `OpenStruct` (id + `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`) and does not read/apply any params, so a `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` would indeed be a no-op that returns 200. However, the added admin UI template (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) never calls `saveChanges`, and host persistence is handled via the separate `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`resources :embeddable_hosts`), so this no-op endpoint appears unused/placeholder rather than a demonstrated broken feature in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `_hydrateEmbedded` in `store.js.es6` now matches any `*_ids` key on every model, deleting raw ids and replacing them with a junk array (e.g. [undefined]) when the subtype isn't registered — shape drift for existing consumers; delete should be conditional on successful hydration

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded` now matches keys ending in `_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and, for the plural case, always maps the id list to `_lookupSubType(...)` results and then unconditionally deletes the original `obj[k]` (`delete obj[k];`). If the subtype lookup fails (e.g. subtype not registered / not present in `root`), the mapped array will contain `undefined` elements, and because arrays are always truthy `hydrated || []` will not replace it with `[]`. This both removes the raw ids and replaces them with a potentially junk array, which is a behavioral regression compared to the singular `_id` branch that only deletes when hydration succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` yields nil for unknown ids and then calls `host.host = ...` / `host.destroy` on nil, producing NoMethodError 500s instead of 404s

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration inserts unescaped host strings via raw SQL interpolation in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25-27`; a host value containing a single quote breaks or corrupts the migration

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on sites without an 'embed_category' site setting, as execute(...)[0]['id'] indexes nil when the result set is empty (same pattern for uncategorized_category_id and embeddable_hosts[0]['value'] lookups); guard each execute result for zero rows before indexing

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration inserts host values verbatim without normalization (e.g. 'http://eviltrout.com'), but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) against the URI host and before_validation never runs for migration-inserted rows, so embedding silently breaks for sites with protocol/path in configured hosts; migration must strip protocol/path the same way the model does

adjudication_records.issue_text: _lookupSubType failures leak false into hydrated arrays in store.js.es6: the plural branch maps ids and assigns the array unconditionally, so failed subtype lookups put false entries into embeddable_colors that consumers iterate over; the plural branch should filter like the singular branch guards if (hydrated)

Since the singular branch explicitly guards `if (hydrated)` before assigning/deleting, `_lookupSubType` can return a falsey value on lookup failure; in the plural branch those falsey values will remain as entries in the array and the original ids are removed, producing arrays containing `false`/`null`/`undefined` that downstream code may iterate over as if they were records.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration is irreversible/misplaced: data migration (SELECT/INSERT/DELETE of site settings) inside change means rake db:rollback fails partway and deleted settings are unrecoverable; should be an up/down migration that reinserts settings on down, and the DELETE destroys the only backup of the host list before verifying rows migrated cleanly

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host validation regex permits ports/paths but lookup ignores them: regex allows :8080 and /path, before_validation strips only protocol and path (not port), and record_for_host compares the full stored host string against uri.host (which excludes port), so a host saved as example.com:8080 passes validation but can never match any referer; either strip the port in normalization or compare on port-stripped values

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and optional path, but the `before_validation` normalization only strips protocol and path (`sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`) and does not strip the port. Later, `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, but `uri.host` excludes the port. adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin update action 500s (NoMethodError) on unknown id because EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first returns nil and is passed to save_host; same pattern in destroy — should be 404

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead guard `hydrated || []` in _hydrateEmbedded plural branch since .map always returns an array; also inconsistent deletion behavior between singular and plural hydration branches

In JavaScript, `String#replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence, so a model type like `foo_bar_baz` would become `foo-bar_baz` and would not match an `ADMIN_MODELS` entry written as `foo-bar-baz`. The diff only adds `embeddable-host` (single underscore case), so nothing in this PR is broken today, but the implementation is a real edge-case/maintainability concern introduced by this change.

Later lookups (`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`) parse the referer URL and query by bare `uri.host` (`where("lower(host) = ?", host)`), so any migrated rows stored as `http://...` or with `/path` will not match and will cause `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` to return false (leading to `invalid referer host`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on fresh installs or sites that never set embed_category because execute(...)[0]['id'] raises NoMethodError when the site_settings row is missing

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for the `embed_category` lookup. If the query returns no rows (e.g., the `site_settings` table has no `embed_category` row), `execute(...)[0]` is nil and `['id']` raises `NoMethodError`. The same pattern is used when falling back to `uncategorized_category_id` (`...[0]['value']`). This is a verifiable crash path based on the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Destructive migration deletes embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings rows with no rollback path, permanently losing admin data if reverted; also create_table force: true silently drops pre-existing table

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which would drop an existing `embeddable_hosts` table if it already exists, and it also executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`. Because this is in a `change` method with raw `execute` calls, there is no defined rollback path to restore those deleted setting rows if the migration is reverted. This is a concrete, diff-grounded data-retention concern, though it primarily impacts rollback/revert scenarios rather than normal forward migrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection / breakage via direct string interpolation of host values in backfill INSERT; should use quote_value/sanitize_sql or EmbeddableHost.create!
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags SQL injection risk caused by directly interpolating host values into an SQL INSERT and recommends using quoting/sanitization or model-based creation, which matches the golden issue about interpolation ('#{h}') in the controller SQL and the need for parameter binding/proper quoting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill doesn't guard against missing uncategorized_category_id fallback row, using same unguarded [0]['value'] pattern that can raise NoMethodError

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the fallback path does `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i`. If that query returns 0 rows (e.g., row missing/corrupt), `[0]` is `nil` and `['value']` will raise `NoMethodError`, causing the migration to fail. There is no guard around the `[0]` access, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on fresh installs: `execute("...WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes a row exists; on fresh installs `[0]` is nil raising NoMethodError, and the same unguarded pattern repeats for the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id']` for the `embed_category` lookup and later `execute(...)[0]['value']` for `uncategorized_category_id`. If either query returns zero rows, `execute(...)[0]` will be `nil`, causing a `NoMethodError` when indexing with `['id']`/`['value']`. The diff shows no guard for empty results, so the migration can crash in that case (e.g., when those site_settings rows don’t exist).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrated embeddable hosts are inserted verbatim via SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization (stripping protocol/path), so stored values like `http://eviltrout.com` will never match `record_for_host`'s host comparison, silently rejecting all existing embed hosts after upgrade

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, existing `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` entries are copied with raw SQL: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` (verbatim `h`). This bypasses `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. Later, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, which will not match rows stored as `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`. Given prior behavior/tests allowed protocols/paths, this can silently break existing allowed hosts after upgrade.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection/crash risk in migration: `#{h}` is interpolated directly into SQL without quoting, so a host value containing a single quote breaks the migration or injects SQL

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds raw SQL with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` comes from a stored setting value and is interpolated directly into a single-quoted SQL string without escaping/parameterization, a host containing a single quote will break the SQL (migration crash) and could allow SQL injection during migration execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddableHostsController#update`/`#destroy` crash on unknown id: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can be nil, and `save_host(nil)` / `nil.destroy` raise 500s
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same problem: update/destroy fetch an EmbeddableHost with `.where(...).first` which can return nil for an unknown id, and subsequent calls (`save_host`/`destroy`) on nil cause a server error (NoMethodError/500).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddingController#update` is a silent no-op: it re-serializes `@embedding` without persisting anything while the frontend save button calls `update({})`, so future template fields will appear to save while writing nothing

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`, so there is nothing persisted on PUT. On the frontend, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would hit that no-op PUT and get a “successful” response. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template does not invoke `saveChanges` (it only adds hosts, which are saved via `EmbeddableHost#save`), so this is more of an incomplete/stubbed endpoint that could mislead future UI work rather than a currently broken behavior shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plural hydration in `_hydrateEmbedded` silently discards data on lookup failure: map produces undefined entries, unconditionally writes `obj[pluralize(subType)]` and deletes the raw key, with no failure detection, no guard that `obj[k]` is an array, and unreachable `|| []` masking the failure

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` + `if (m[2])`) does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(..._lookupSubType...)` and then unconditionally assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated` and `delete obj[k]`. Unlike the singular branch (which only deletes the raw `*_id` when `hydrated` is truthy), this always deletes the original `*_ids` even when `_lookupSubType` returns nothing for one or more ids, leaving `undefined` entries and losing the original ids. It also assumes `obj[k]` is an array (`.map`) with no guard. The `|| []` is ineffective because `.map` always returns an Array (truthy), so it won’t surface/handle lookup failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavior change in embed authorization: no-hosts state now rejects all requests with misleading 'invalid referer host' error instead of the previous distinct 'embeddable hosts not set' error, a diagnosability regression

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the explicit check/exception for `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` (raising `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable hosts not set')`) was removed and replaced with a single check `unless EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` that raises `'invalid referer host'` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). Since `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` returns false when there are no records, the no-hosts-configured state now yields the same `'invalid referer host'` error, reducing diagnosability compared to the previous distinct message. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior/message regression but not a clear functional correctness break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `expandable_first_post?` in topic.rb loosened: now any topic with a `topic_embed` can be expandable regardless of current host config, a silent semantics change

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb). Since the `embeddable_hosts` site setting was removed/migrated to the `EmbeddableHost` table, this drops the “embedding enabled/hosts configured” gate entirely, so existing topics with a `topic_embed` can still be treated as expandable even if no allowed hosts are configured. That is a real, diff-grounded semantics change, but whether it’s incorrect vs. intended isn’t provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled failure path in delete flow: `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch` so failed DELETEs give no feedback; also `Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)` may return null in save() leaving `host.category` null in UI while server state differs

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` without any `.catch(...)`, unlike `save()` which explicitly `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. A failed DELETE will therefore surface as an unhandled promise rejection and provide no user feedback, and `deleteHost` won’t be invoked, leaving the UI in an inconsistent/silent-failure state. The note about `Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)` potentially returning `null` in `save()` is plausible from the code path (`host.set('category', ...)`), but depends on whether categories are guaranteed loaded; the missing delete error handling is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Category fabricators relocated into misleadingly named files: `category_fabricator.rb` defines `:embeddable_host` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines the `:category` fabricators, which is easy to break and confusing

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (and no longer defines `:category`), while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)` and related category variants. This file/fabricator-name swap is confusing and easy to break for future contributors, even if it may not immediately fail tests as long as all fabricator files are glob-required.
